CURRENT AUTHORIZED SCOPE (2026-11-25 user clarification; supersedes conflicting planning-only and adapter-prerequisite wording): Implement the generic capability-driven foundation and adaptive SMTP in this PR. No external repository edits, newer Mattermost/Jido integration, mix.exs or pin changes, or local dependency substitution. Extend existing EmailBridge SMTP declaration; keep existing Jido/Web behavior conservative without metadata. Use compatible test adapters to prove declarations. External adapter work is follow-up, not a blocker. No new callbacks/modules/frameworks; existing capability_snapshot path, CommunicationBridge, FileSettings/Ecto, TransportRequirements.resolve, authorized saves and shared components remain owners. Preserve limited exact SMTP additive metadata test approval only; other test gates and human UX approval remain. No commits, pushes, merges or publication.

Current coding-agent handoff — capability-driven communication configuration (2026-11-25)
STATUS: Planning only. User approved the design direction, not coding. Do not implement until explicitly instructed. This description supersedes earlier proposed names/shapes and conflicting task wording. Keep historical comments as history; verify claims against live source. At audit HEAD 2107c75e5, the existing shared components, FileSettings and TransportRequirements.resolve/2 are already present.

Outcome
All three communication bridges translate selected-adapter facts into one normalized contract owned by CommunicationBridge. BO displays applicable Advanced settings and Engine rejects invalid configuration using one shared Ecto-backed implementation. Preserve the existing capability modal wiring and existing settings semantics.

Approved contract and invariants
- Preserve kind, required, resolved, unsupported and labels, including existing keys/status meanings. Do not rename resolved to features or capabilities. Top-level required remains the capability inventory, not required form fields.
- Extend existing file_delivery with transfer_mode, supports_attachment_edits and limits. Limits retain value/configurable/required and gain known type/unit/validation metadata. Normalize/project these additions through the existing FileSettings metadata helpers; otherwise they will be dropped.
- CommunicationBridge owns communication normalization. Generic Bridge owns provider/config selection and dispatch by kind; data-source semantics remain intact. Concrete bridges own adapter vocabulary translation only, not separate normalization, defaulting, validation or TransportRequirements construction.
- Transport facts, user overrides and ZAQ failure policy remain separate. Mattermost file_requirements.max_file_size is configured/effective, not a discovered provider ceiling. Unknown facts remain unresolved; only declared inapplicability becomes not_applicable. Missing metadata cannot grant support.
- Required configuration is enforced only for usable file support (native/fallback/true), not merely because a connector is enabled. Required means a valid effective value: a declared fixed value can satisfy it; an unresolved required configurable value needs input. Preserve unsupported SMTP blank-settings behavior.
- Save settings.file_delivery, positive integer bytes/count and send_on_file_failure only; no derived requirements or capability snapshot persistence. Preserve exact decimal MB, optional blank clearing, omitted values, explicit false and unrelated settings.

Mandatory reuse map — extend these owners
1. Existing bridge capability_snapshot/1 producers, Bridge.capability_snapshot/2 and :channel_capability_snapshot event. CommunicationBridge.normalize_capability_snapshot/2 is the communication normalization owner. Do not introduce a second snapshot pipeline or new bridge file-specific callback.
2. ConnectorConfig.FileSettings: metadata/1 and existing metadata validators/normalizer; supported?/2, visible?/1, limit/2; normalize_form/1, merge_form/2, form_values/1; validate/2, validate_changeset/3, effective_limits/2; add_errors/3 and errors/1. Reuse these entry points; Ecto replaces applicable internal validation, not an additional competing validation layer.
3. Channels.TransportRequirements.resolve/2 already exists. Extend it only if needed, preserving struct fields/defaults/enforced keys and return/error contracts. Never add TransportRequirementsResolver or a second builder.
4. ChannelConfig.changeset/2 and existing persistence preparation; EmailConnectorSettings.save/2; LiveUpdateSettings.execute existing grouped save; WidgetConnectorSettings.execute/2 and its allowlist/projection/persistence. Reuse their existing authorized Actions: SaveEmailConnector, ManageLiveUpdateSettings, ManageWidgetConnector. Preserve NodeRouter/Event, actor, archive/provider/kind, revision/locking, encryption and rollback boundaries. Do not create another save service, Action, preview endpoint or agent tool.
5. Components.ConnectionSettings.editor/1, tab_for_errors/2, switch_settings_tab/2; FileDeliverySettings.section/1, form_params/2 and errors/1; LiveUpdateSettings.fields/1 with embedded mode; ChannelCapabilities.icon_with_modal/1. Reuse DesignSystem.Input, Switch and the current modal shell. No new file-settings component, tab system, duplicate labels/units/defaults, inline duplicate markup or provider-specific BO conditions.
6. Existing SettingsTest, TransportRequirementsTest, Bridge/CommunicationBridge/API tests, ChannelConfig/EmailConnectorSettings/WidgetConnectorSettings suites, FileDeliverySettings/ConnectionSettings suites and existing LiveView/Storybook/browser fixtures. Extend relevant owning suites; do not create parallel suites or copy tests from PR6/other worktrees.

Rules against drift
Before adding any function, including private helpers, inspect existing candidates/callers and record why reuse or extension does not fit. Prefer extension with compatible defaults. A focused private helper in its existing owner may be justified by coherent responsibility; no blanket ban that forces unreadable functions. A new public module/API/component requires concrete missing ownership/contract evidence and a proposed plan amendment before implementation. No generic capability registry, rule engine, schema framework, dynamic atom creation or adapter-supplied executable validators. Treat metadata as data and allowlist supported fields/types/rules. Remove superseded logic once callers share the owner; compatibility wrappers must delegate, not retain independent algorithms. Reuse module responsibilities, not merely similar syntax.

Sequence and owning tasks
A. zaq-h2i.3.1 establishes the declaration contract using current sources; zaq-h2i.4 owns later external adapter implementation/releases and does not block this PR. No new dependencies, local substitutions or source callbacks. Current Jido/Web retain existing behavior without metadata; compatible bridge fixtures prove integration. SMTP extends its existing EmailBridge declaration.
B. zaq-h2i.3.8: extend common normalization and bridge declaration translation with real-producer tests.
C. zaq-h2i.3.2: extend FileSettings with Ecto-backed validation and existing resolver consumers. Keep exact conversion and domain-only constraints in their owners.
D. zaq-h2i.3.9: validate effective proposed connection on creation/update/enablement through existing persistence operations, removing unchanged-file bypass. Do not reload only the old config or trust a stale BO snapshot for final validation.
E. zaq-h2i.3.3: finish existing channel/SMTP UI and capability-conditional widget wiring. Widget needs its existing request allowlist, selected projection, drafts, persistence and error mapping extended together.
F. Existing validation/UX/E2E tasks zaq-h2i.3.6, zaq-h2i.3.4, zaq-h2i.3.5. The executable issue sequence is recorded below and its dependency links are materialized. Do not start coding without explicit user authorization.

BO behavior
Reuse single parent form with inactive panels mounted; preserve SMTP transport, widget identity/routing and streamed-update controls. Show declared configurable inputs, fixed read-only values and unresolved/not-applicable states. Compute required indicators/help from the same effective rules as save validation. Do not indiscriminately attach HTML required to hidden controls and prevent submit/error-tab selection. Preserve errors/drafts and select the proper tab after rejected saves.
Distinguish successful empty/unsupported snapshots from lookup failures. Reuse capability recovery state/helpers and existing feedback components; show/retry errors rather than silently hide configuration. Block mutations that require unavailable validation without changing existing unrelated-save/disabled-widget behavior indiscriminately.
LiveView validate handlers remain assign-only: no DB/network lookup on each keystroke. Cache facts for feedback, invalidate/reload through existing lifecycle/recovery events when relevant inputs change, and let Engine perform authoritative proposed-config validation at Save. Never let stale client-side facts permanently veto a server-valid change.

Validation and scope
Original focused tests prove shared ownership: same declarations through real Jido/Email/Web producer paths; unsupported/unknown/conflicting metadata; exact conversion/ceilings properties; blank/whitespace/false; proposed-config changes and rollback; channel/SMTP/widget save/reload; failed lookup retry; hidden-tab submission/error behavior. Preserve existing assertions unless explicitly approved. Follow workflow owner for mix q, isolated tests, review, coverage and final precommit; new feature E2E waits for human UX approval. Update existing Storybook and service guides, not parallel contract documentation.
PR6 is reference material, not authorization to import delivery stack. Later integration reuses its transport preparation/execution/planner tests, replaces per-bridge requirement construction with shared resolve and explicitly reconciles legacy setting keys/error-policy behavior. No commits/pushes or dependency publication are authorized.

Action reuse: extend existing snapshot/domain validation/authorized save operations; pure normalization/resolution stays local to existing domain owners. Planning changes themselves require no new Action.

Materialized execution graph (2026-11-25)
zaq-h2i.3.1 -> zaq-h2i.3.8 -> zaq-h2i.3.2 -> zaq-h2i.3.9 -> zaq-h2i.3.7 -> zaq-h2i.3.3 -> zaq-h2i.3.11 -> zaq-h2i.3.12 -> zaq-h2i.3.4 -> zaq-h2i.3.5 -> zaq-h2i.3.13
Existing completed tab-layout issue zaq-h2i.3.6 remains closed as reusable foundation. Conflicting unconditional-requirements issue zaq-h2i.3.10 is closed as superseded, not implemented. Dependency links enforce order; consult current issue statuses and verified implementation notes for progress. The in-PR sequence starts with zaq-h2i.3.1; external adapter work zaq-h2i.4 is nonblocking follow-up. Parent's pre-existing external prerequisite zaq-h2i.2 remains unchanged; do not infer its completion from this planning operation.

Task boundaries: zaq-h2i.3.3 owns shared component and channel/SMTP changes; zaq-h2i.3.11 owns widget integration using them. zaq-h2i.3.12 owns final integration review/docs/Storybook before the human UX gate. zaq-h2i.3.13 owns post-review coverage/final precommit under workflow policy after consolidated E2E. No duplicate implementation and no code changes during issue planning.
